output.summary: Reuse the existing CI runner's individual-test balancing for an all-CPU local suite with exact execution accounting, then measure and remove the slowest remaining bottlenecks to meet the owner's five-minute target. Add an opt-in, CPU-budgeted parallel mode for goal/repository command lanes without skipping commands; record integer-millisecond timing with a strictly qualified last-merged-target baseline. The default template passes measured test cost to test review and the Tests lens and shows timing/delta or an explicit unavailable reason at merge approval; this repository adopts the changes through its separately owner-approved policy PR.

spec:
Found while dogfooding Release 1. Owner, verbatim: "Yeah I think we should do sharded test runs, but we also need to be keeping an eye on test run times. Does the test review lens check test run times for sanity?"

Facts (2026-11-02, G1025 branch, 20-core machine):
- run_tests runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents` on one core: about 20 to 25 minutes, up from 11 to 14 minutes earlier the same day; one run hit a 25-minute limit. Machine load stayed under 3.
- The same suite split by file, 12 files at a time, took 491 s, bounded by the two slowest files: test_engine_lenses.py 487 s (62 tests) and test_engine_branching.py 474 s (56 tests). Next: test_engine_github 200 s, test_engine_review_lenses 169 s, test_engine_owner_questions 155 s.
- CI already shards with .github/scripts/run_product_validation.py; locally its discovery failed only because a G1025 test module collected TestCases twice (fixed on G1025).
- Neither the review_tests prompt nor the Tests lens mentions run time, and run_tests' recorded per-command `seconds` are never shown to a reviewer or the owner.
- G1025's run_tests (2026-11-02) took 2,686 s: its recorded test_design command (test_engine_branching.py, 497 s) and then the full suite (2,189 s, single core), which runs that same file again. Owner, verbatim: "This run is 40m and counting...". When verification already runs the full suite, run_tests should not run the targeted commands separately (or should run them in parallel).

Scope:
- One repository command that runs the canonical suite sharded in parallel on the local machine (reusing run_product_validation.py's inventory and balancing, worker count from the CPU count), with a single pass/fail and per-shard timings; this repository's verification.commands use it through a policy PR the owner approves.
- Split or speed up the slowest test files so no single file dominates (target: a full local run under 5 minutes on an 8+ core machine), without weakening what they assert.
- Test cost becomes a reviewed quantity: review_tests and the Tests lens ask for the run time of new or changed tests (from the run, not a guess) and flag disproportionate cost (sleeps, repeated full journeys where a unit check would do, wall-clock bounds); run_tests records per-command and total seconds and the delta against the last run on the integration branch, and approve_merge shows it.
- Keep the engine small: durations are already recorded by checks.run; prefer showing them over new machinery.

Acceptance:
- A full local run of this repository's suite completes in under 5 minutes on the owner's machine and still runs every test once (discovery has no duplicate ids).
- A review_tests card for a goal that adds a slow test shows its measured cost, and the prompt asks the reviewer to judge it.
- The approve_merge item shows run_tests total time and its change versus trunk.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes and adds a HISTORY §4 row.
title: Run local verification sharded, and make test run time a reviewed quantity
